transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Jonas Patel (Redwood SE), Amira Lopez (Redwood Support), Aisha Khan (MeridianPay Head of Platform), Ben Turner (SRE), Liu Chen (ML Eng), Rachel Park (Product)

Summary:
Quick sync on POC latency tuning. Reviewed latest TTFT and streaming results, discussed sequence length distribution, kernel choices and fallback behaviors, agreed next steps for expanded benchmarks and logs to share with infra team. Action items assigned.

Topics:
- TTFT (time to first token) regressions with long-context requests
- Streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs for P50/P95
- Sequence length distribution and effective padding impact
- Kernel selection and quantization impacts on first-token latency
- Next steps: benchmarks, logs, on-prem deep dive

Action items (captured):
- Jonas to collect kernel traces and NV/ROC profiler outputs
- Aisha to provide request histograms and representative payloads
- Sofia to send cost/runbook + kernel recommendations

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick check-in today on the latency tuning work for the meridian pay pilot, we've got about 45 minutes, agenda is TTFT and streaming, then kernels and next steps.
[00:18] Aisha: sounds good, thanks. ben and liu are on in case we hit infra questions.
[00:22] Jonas: great, i'll start with the numbers we ran last night, so we ran the 512 and 2048 token mixes with streaming on and off, the TTFT P50 for streaming was 82ms on our dedicated pool, P95 was 210ms, without streaming P50 was about 140ms. so streaming definitely helps TTFT but we saw some noisier tails.
[00:45] Ben: when you say dedicated, that's redwood dedicated gpu pool with the nvlink nodes?
[00:50] Jonas: yes, gpus with nvlink; on our side used the small batch low-latency config, quantization set to int8 for the large model variant.
[01:05] Liu: quick clarifying Q  are you using prefix KV cache for repeated sessions? that was our big hope to reduce repeat prompt latency.
[01:12] Jonas: yep we enabled prefix KV cache for the chat scenario, we saw amortized token cost go down about 12% for repeated conversations, but the very first token still depends on kernel boot and memory touches.
[01:27] Aisha: we noticed yesterday some requests where TTFT spiked to 600ms, is that related to sequence length or cold kernels?
[01:35] Jonas: likely a mix  long sequence length means more attention kernel setup and the runtime switches to a different kernel path for >1024 tokens which appears to have a higher setup cost. also possible page faults on cache miss.
[01:50] Sofia: are these spikes reproducible with the same request sample?
[01:55] Jonas: some were reproducible, others were intermittent. i'm collecting kernel traces (nvprof/rocprof) to pinpoint whether it’s memory allocation / kernel selection overhead vs scheduling.
[02:10] Rachel: from product perspective, our SLO is 200ms TTFT p95 for customer-facing flows; anything above that degrades UX.
[02:18] Sofia: okay that's helpful, we'll optimize for that target. two quick follow ups: (1) we can tune streaming chunk sizes  smaller chunks improve TTFT but increase total tokens and overhead; (2) kernel prewarming and pinned memory options might reduce cold-starts.
[02:40] Ben: on the infra side we can reserve pinned pages but need a cost estimate, do you have guidance?
[02:46] Jonas: rough numbers in the config doc  pinned memory for a dedicated node adds about 8-12% memory overhead per model instance, but reduces page faults and first token latency. we'll include exact numbers in the kernel logs.
[03:02] Liu: another variable is input tokenization variance  our users sometimes send batch of short prompts and then occasional long bios which cause padding overhead and slow down.
[03:12] Jonas: right  padding inflation is real; if your histogram shows many short requests, batching strategy can be aggressive; for mixed distributions we recommend adaptive batching with max-seq grouping.
[03:28] Aisha: i'll send our request histogram, we have a lot around 64-128 tokens but 2-3% at >1500 tokens.
[03:35] Sofia: that’s good to know  the 2-3% long tails can dominate p95 unless we route those to a cheaper variant or different node.
[03:45] Jonas: one practical thing we tested: we tried model variant with quantization to int8+peft and it improved throughput, but i noticed TTFT slightly worsened due to extra dequant/decode steps in the first token path.
[04:00] Ben: is that reversible by changing kernel ordering? like use a fast small-kernel for first token and then switch?
[04:06] Jonas: conceptually yes, but switching kernels within a request adds complexity; some runtimes do a hybrid approach  preselect small-kernel for TTFT and then stream large-kernel outputs, but it's tradeoff.
[04:20] Aisha: any implication for our private deployment? we need on-prem option for regulated flows.
[04:26] Sofia: behavior is similar on private, though kernel and driver versions matter a lot. you should expect driver-level diffs to affect TTFT. we'll want your infra team to run the same profiler traces.
[04:38] Liu: ok we can run the profiler, what's easiest for us to collect?
[04:43] Jonas: we'll share a small script that wraps nvprof/rocprof commands and filters the relevant kernel timestamps. i'll attach it after the call.
[04:52] Rachel: about streaming chunk size  what did you test?
[04:56] Jonas: we tested 32 token chunks and 8 token chunks. 32 token gave a P50 of 82ms, 8 token lowers P50 to 70ms but increased total compute by ~6% and increased P95 noise because of more context switches.
[05:15] Aisha: given our SLO, maybe 16 token chunks is a good middle ground?
[05:19] Sofia: agree, 16 is often a sweet spot for many customers. we'll recommend 16 and run a follow up benchmark.
[05:27] Ben: curious about background eviction  are you seeing any KV cache evictions impacting latency?
[05:34] Jonas: some, especially when multiple sessions spike concurrently; we observed cache churn when memory pressure hits. pinning or increasing the cache quota helps.
[05:45] Aisha: can we have redwood set up a route policy so long sequences are routed to dedicated high-mem nodes?
[05:52] Sofia: yes, routing by max_seq is a common policy; we can implement a canary and roll it in for the pilot.
[06:00] Liu: quick question on metrics  what telemetry do you collect for TTFT?
[06:05] Jonas: we record time to request accepted, time to first byte, kernel launch time, and token emit times. we'll share the mapping to your existing prometheus metrics.
[06:15] Aisha: perfect.
[06:18] Sofia: ok next, troubleshooting the 600ms spike  jonas, can you talk through what you'd need from meridian?
[06:24] Jonas: i'll need the raw request that produced the spike, the exact model variant, and driver/kernel versions. if you can reproduce on your on-prem, capture nvprof; if not we can try to reproduce on dedicated and correlate.
[06:38] Aisha: we'll pull the logs and send sample requests. ben and liu will collaborate.
[06:44] Jonas: thanks.
[06:46] Rachel: any legal/security asks here? we did request SOC2 docs last week.
[06:50] Sofia: yes we'll send SOC2 and data handling docs after this call, also the pilot contract addendum.
[06:57] Aisha: good. also curious if there are any known regressions in the last runtime patch?
[07:02] Jonas: there was a kernel scheduling tweak two weeks ago that improved throughput but introduced a corner case with long sequences; we've got a patch queued and we'll test it against your samples.
[07:16] Ben: can the patch be toggled per node? we'd like a canary.
[07:20] Jonas: yes, we can toggle via rollout policy and route a subset of traffic.
[07:26] Sofia: let's plan a canary once we have the profiler traces and request histograms.
[07:31] Aisha: timeline wise, we'd like production pilot by early nov so we need the config locked by end of october.
[07:38] Sofia: that's achievable assuming benchmarks finish this week.
[07:42] Jonas: i'll run the 10k-token long-tail benchmark overnight and share results tomorrow, and i will include the kernel logs for both streaming chunk sizes 8/16/32.
[07:53] Liu: on our side i'll provision a test node and run the nvprof script, expect to send results by friday.
[07:59] Sofia: perfect.
[08:02] Amira: i'll add the action items in the support ticket and link kernel logs and the cost projection doc.
[08:08] Rachel: any tradeoffs we should call out for product?
[08:12] Sofia: main tradeoffs  smaller streaming chunks reduce TTFT but raise compute and token overhead; quantization improves throughput but may worsen first-token latency; kernel prewarming reduces spikes but costs memory/pinned pages; routing long sequences to high-mem nodes preserves p95 at cost of capacity.
[08:34] Aisha: noted.
[08:36] Jonas: one extra note  for private deployments driver and kernel versions must be synced with our runtime; small diffs in CUDA/ROCm cause pretty different timings.
[08:48] Ben: we'll coordinate versions.
[08:50] Sofia: okay let's recap next steps  jonas runs 10k-token benchmark and attaches kernel traces (due 10/25), aisha sends histograms and sample requests (due 10/22), sofia shares cost/projection and kernel recommendations (due 10/23), schedule on-prem deep dive week of 10/26.
[09:10] Aisha: thanks all, that works.
[09:13] Sofia: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the ticket and share docs.
[44:20] call end: 16:45 PT
